results.summary: I rebuilt the repair commit 9e2e3a8a in my own scratch copy (a sparse, shared clone; nothing in the tksCAS repo was touched). I ran its three acceptance scripts and then checked every number in its README a second way. Every count reproduces exactly: base 86 pass / 117 fail, peer a4b2e0d7 111 pass / 92 fail, repaired 203 pass / 0 fail. Pytest collection and ast parsing give 39 + 12 + 19 = 70 test functions and 39 + 12 + 152 = 203 test cases. My own replay reached the same results without the runner's special pytest flags. I also compared each test body byte-for-byte with ast.get_source_segment. All 39 original bodies match eb998556, and all 12 carried bodies match a4b2e0d7 (the whole test_quantifiers.py blob is identical, ca8aa5b7). 9 of those 12 were already identical at 86ba3d75. The repaired refusals fail for the intended reason: all 113 cases that expect an error raise a named ValueError (109) or InadmissibleTrendError, which is a subclass of ValueError (4), from explicit raise lines. The census also holds: 1,052 other test_*.py files, and no other tracked test imports api.cas_ohm. I found three small, new problems (P3), and none of them changes any number. (1) On this machine's default Git setting (core.autocrlf=true, set in the system gitconfig), the README's 'reproduce' steps fail, because the .py/.md package files come out with Windows line endings (CRLF). (2) The runner creates its temp folder two levels above the repository root, which is outside the repository. (3) The runner's own `-c os.devnull` flag strips file names from the raw pytest logs and XML. One more point: 37 of the 117 base failures are cases where the old code already stopped with a different error type (OverflowError, TypeError, InvalidOperation and similar). They are not cases of the old code silently returning a bad number. The README does not claim otherwise.

results.summary: I re-ran the peer audit's own failing probes, with their logic unchanged, against the frozen source 626cc84b and against the repair 9e2e3a8a. At 626cc84b both peer scripts behave exactly as the audit recorded. contract_boundary_probes.py gives 8 tests with 7 failures and 1 error (a ZeroDivisionError), exit 1. audit_ohm.py rebuilds its committed results.json and CLAIM_VERDICTS.json byte for byte (results.json sha256 1e796e85...). At 9e2e3a8a all 8 contract probes pass (exit 0), and each one passes for the intended reason: a named ValueError or InadmissibleTrendError, or a CensoredResult with a named marker. None passes because of an accidental TypeError. Of the 50 audit_ohm probes, all 43 that belong to the numbered findings OHM-A1 to A7 or to their valid controls now behave as the peer asked. The other 7 are the peer's side observations: eligibility accepting None or 'false', the default ACTIVE region, and bare floats and unvalidated trace records. The repair left those 7 unchanged and says so in its own limits. My own extra variant tests found no hidden gaps behind the fixes, with one exception. The switch to exact decimal and fraction arithmetic (the fix for A5 and A6) lets a finite input with a huge exponent run slowly or produce a huge string: 6.112-9.441 s for exponent 1E+10000000, and past a 90 s timeout at 1E+100000000. I also found five small inherited gaps and confirmed that the two peer side observations above are still open. All are P3 (low priority); none is a P1 or P2 defect in the repair.

results.label: adversary-numeric
results.summary:
I attacked every public function of the repaired quantifiers.py (9e2e3a8a) with 1,000+ adversarial calls and ran each case against a4b2e0d7 as well, to tell new problems from old ones. What the repair claims mostly holds up. Its own 203 tests pass. NaN, infinity, sNaN, int overflow and the overflow cases 1e308-(-1e308) and 1/5e-324 are now refused with ValueError or censored. Saved maturity values replay into the same band: I tried 99 cut-point values under 9 tampered Decimal contexts plus a fresh thread, with 0 mismatches (a4b2 had 1,477 problems). Import no longer changes global Decimal precision: it stays 28 before and after (a4b2 changed it from 28 to 50). Small positive values and signed residuals still work in the float functions.

I found one serious new defect. The repair now builds exact fractions (Fraction) from any previous level or trend point. A 25-character Decimal such as D('1E-999999999999999999') therefore makes maturity_q4 and admissible_trend hang with no limit. The call was still running when killed at 60 s. The stack sits in fractions.py __new__, called from quantifiers.py line 713 or line 807. At a4b2 the same calls returned instantly. Time grows faster than the exponent: 1E-1000000 takes 0.138 s, 1E-3000000 takes 0.715 s and 1E+10000000 takes 7.110 s. For a very tiny or very huge current level with no previous level, the repair raises a raw MemoryError at line 724. That is not the documented ValueError.

The other defects are older (inherited) or small. r_total accepts four parts whose exact sum is zero or negative, because float rounding leaves a positive residue. check_eligibility admits when stale is None, when outcome is None, or when outcome is the string 'UNASSESSED'. The peer audit already reported this and the repair README says these gaps stay open. r_hidden accepts a negative point observation and returns a negative apparent resistance, although the same observation given as an interval is censored. For a wholly negative interval, the censoring message falsely says the interval 'includes or touches zero'. r_hidden and admissible_trend treat the text '12' as the interval (1,2), and b'12' as (49,50). The new underflow guard is skipped for str and Fraction inputs. The new point-inside-interval check compares rounded floats, so a point that is exactly outside can be admitted. A few more small type and precision gaps are listed below. Each is labelled with its status at a4b2.

results.label: adversary-contract
results.summary: The repair (9e2e3a8a, same tree as 34b0d982) mostly changed only what NUMERIC_POLICY.md says. I found no hidden clamping, no new rounding, and no swallowed errors. All 11 public function signatures are unchanged. The only new result field is minimum_effect_exact, added at the end of MaturityQ4 and TrendTag. The 51 old test bodies are byte-identical, and the compiler helper files are untouched. I ran two seeded grids of mostly valid inputs (43,134 cases and 36,566 boundary cases) against a4b2e0d7 and the repair. The repair never disagreed with the policy's exact-arithmetic rule (0 disagreements in 21,376 trend checks, 19,563 maturity-trend checks and 21,376 band checks). Almost every difference maps to a policy bullet. But I found six undocumented changes: -0.0 thresholds are no longer turned into 0.0; r_cap now accepts Decimal bounds and returns float where it used to return int; True is now refused as a maturity/trend threshold; results built by hand no longer compare equal to returned results; one zero-compatible Decimal observation loses the marker the policy promises to keep; and one new cost problem. That cost problem is the most important: exact fractions are now built from level and point inputs without a size check, so a 12-character Decimal like 1E-100000000 makes maturity_q4 run for more than 60 seconds, where a4 took 0.000s. Signed residuals stay signed, tiny positive values still work, and zero observed flow still gives a negative residual with the ratio censored, all confirmed by running.

Issue 1 (breakdown) is real, and it was created by the OD-A edit 0fc6bb30. Appendix B:59 and :79 now say the involution flip happens only when an explicit rule is declared.
